descriptions.job-0bndogh:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Product Accounting team at Stripe supports products across Stripe by providing guidance on accounting implications and enabling teams to make informed strategic decisions. The team records business transactions accurately and on time in the balance sheet and income statement, and partners with cross-functional and international teams in a fast-paced environment.

What you’ll do

Stripe is seeking an experienced accountant to join our world-class accounting team, focusing on products developed by our Bridge subsidiary. You’ll leverage your technical expertise with U.S. GAAP to identify accounting implications and customer impacts and advise cross-functional partners. You will be responsible for ensuring timely and accurate month-end close results for Bridge products, while also working on initiatives to create scalable accounting solutions.. 

Responsibilities

  • Plan and perform monthly close activities, including journal entries, reconciliations, analytic reviews, and financial reporting deliverables for Bridge products
  • Identify, recommend and implement scalable accounting processes to support global growth at Bridge
  • Partner with our business and finance teams to understand new products, features, and contracts, and advise on accounting implications
  • Partner with Internal Systems and Engineering teams to improve financial systems and automate accounting processes
  • Assess the effectiveness of internal controls and design processes and controls for emerging business activities
  • Understand data and system flows, analyzing financial results to identify and address anomalies.
  • Support external audit processes

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 7+ years of relevant public accounting and/or industry experience
  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field
  • Professional accountancy qualification, such as CA, CPA, ACA, ACCA, or CIMA
  • Working knowledge of US GAAP and experience with internal controls
  • Experience with monthly or quarterly close processes, journal-entry preparation and posting, audits, regulatory reporting, financial-statement preparation, and accounting systems
  • Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills, with the ability to convey financial concepts to both financial and non-financial audiences
  • Ability to structure ambiguous work and build systems and automation 
  • Demonstrated experience partnering with cross-functional stakeholders

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience in the technology or payments industry
  • Experience accounting for cryptocurrencies, including stablecoins
  • Experience with Oracle Suite
  • Experience with data-querying and analysis tools, including SQL
descriptions.job-10l0a4x:
Building the Future of Open Finance

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.


Before you apply, we encourage you to explore our culture page to understand what drives us and how we work.

The team

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

This is a fully remote role, for a US-licensed attorney, preferably based on the West Coast, to join Payward’s world class in-house legal department, reporting to the Global Head of Labor & Employment.

 

The opportunity

  • Serve as a senior member of the Labor and Employment (L&E) legal team, sharing the day-to-day workload with the Global Head of L&E and the broader team

  • Work with executive leadership, existing employment counsel, Payward Experience (PX), and other teams to develop L&E practices for rapidly growing global/worldwide workforce

  • Advise the company on worker classification issues, employee separations, executive compensation agreements, compensation plans, and wage-and-hour matters

  • Advise the company on risk mitigation for trade secret matters, and restrictive covenants

  • Support employment and labor due diligence for M&A transactions and advise on post-closing workforce integration, including harmonizing employment terms, policies, and compensation and benefits programs across acquired employee populations

  • Provide expert strategic input to the business and recruiting teams on expanding Payward’s global footprint, including EOR and direct employment decisions, transitions between EOR, direct employment, and contractor models for new markets and acquired workforces, global mobility, contingent workforce, and the related worker classification risks

  • Work closely with the PX team and business leaders to craft on-point policies and procedures, and to develop and deliver related manager and employee training, for a successful global/worldwide workplace

  • Advise on data privacy issues affecting employees and candidates

  • Support the PX team with global workplace investigations and employee relations matters involving whistleblower allegations, discrimination, and personnel performance issues

  • Manage outside counsel on pre-litigation, arbitration, and local-law matters, and coordinate with litigation counsel on employment disputes

  • Help build and refine AI-enabled workflows for the L&E team, such as contract review, policy drafting, and diligence, and set practical guardrails for their use

  • Monitor and advise on global L&E trends including those within the cryptocurrency industry to help Company’s competitive adaptability, talent acquisition and retention, and workplace processes

  • Additional duties and responsibilities as assigned

 

What you bring

  • 10+ years of legal experience advising in the US and other jurisdictions on Employment, Labor, and Executive Compensation issues, to include in-house and law-firm experience working with companies in both high-growth scaling and mature, large-enterprise environments

  • Broad international Labor and Employment background - law and drafting

  • Flexibility to work hours that overlap with PX team members and Asia-Pacific colleagues

  • Experience with due diligence and related ramifications when making acquisitions, including post-closing workforce integration

  • Experience with compensation plans and with data privacy issues affecting employees and candidates

  • Active license to practice law in at least one US State, or eligibility to practice as registered in-house counsel

  • Hands-on proficiency using generative AI tools (such as Claude or ChatGPT) in day-to-day legal work, with sound judgment on verifying outputs and protecting confidentiality, privilege, and personal data

  • A proactive, entrepreneurial mindset, plus an opportunity-making attitude, using the law to increase the company’s optionality, not decrease it

 

Nice to haves

  • Interest in the crypto industry / what our company is offering to the world and why

  • Experience in fintech, crypto, or other regulated financial services industries

  • Experience in Asian and/or Latin American employment markets

 
 
 

Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution.

We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

Our commitment

Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. We hire based on merit, seeking out people with the right abilities, knowledge, and skills for the job. We encourage you to apply for roles where you don't fully meet the listed requirements, especially if you're passionate or knowledgeable about crypto.

We may ask candidates to complete job-related skills or work-style assessments as part of our hiring process. These assessments evaluate competencies relevant to the role and are applied consistently across candidates for similar positions. Results are considered alongside experience and interviews, and are not the sole basis for any employment decision.

As an equal opportunity employer, we don't tolerate discrimination or harassment of any kind, whether based on race, ethnicity, age, gender identity, citizenship, religion, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws.

descriptions.job-0s1phxt:
Hex Trust is a fully-licensed and insured digital asset custodian. Led by veteran banking technologists and award-winning financial services experts, Hex Trust has built Hex Safe, a proprietary bank-grade platform that delivers solutions for digital asset protocols, foundations, financial institutions, and the Web3 ecosystem. Hex Trust has offices in Singapore, Hong Kong, Dubai, Italy, and Vietnam.

Position Summary

The Personal Assistant / Executive Assistant provides high-level personal and administrative support to executive leadership. In this role, you will manage daily executive operations, complex scheduling, travel arrangements, and key communications, while also maintaining efficient day-to-day administrative support for the office.

This role requires a proactive, highly organized individual who excels at multitasking, executive assistance, and seamless operational support.

Duties & Responsibilities

1. Executive Support & Partnership (EA Scope)

  • Calendar & Time Management: Manage and optimize the executive’s complex calendar, prioritizing high-value engagements and managing competing requests.
  • Strategic Communication: Serve as the primary point of contact and gatekeeper between executive leadership, internal teams, board members, and external stakeholders.
  • Meeting & Board Prep: Organize executive, leadership, and Board of Directors meetings. Draft agendas, compile presentation decks, record meeting minutes, and track follow-up action items.
  • Travel & Expense Management: Coordinate complex international/domestic travel itineraries, logistics, visas, and manage executive expense reconciliation.
  • Project Tracking: Lead or assist with strategic special projects on behalf of the executive, ensuring deliverables stay on timeline.

2. General Administrative & Office Support

  • Administrative Support: Provide day-to-day administrative support across office functions, assisting team members and maintaining organized office procedures.
  • Office Coordination: Assist with physical and virtual office logistics, supplies ordering, facilities coordination, and vendor communications.
  • Workflow Maintenance: Support the upkeep of standardized administrative workflows, filing systems, and document management systems.
  • Expense & Invoice Processing: Assist with office expense tracking, invoice processing, and routine administrative purchasing.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with HR, IT, Finance, and Legal to streamline employee onboarding/offboarding, IT asset distribution, and company policy compliance.
  • Experience: 2–4+ years of experience in a Personal Assistant, Executive Assistant, or Administrative Assistant role.
  • Organizational Skills: Strong administrative capability, experience coordinating schedules and travel, and solid attention to detail.
  • Technical Proficiency: High mastery of executive tools (Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Slack, Zoom) and project management software (Asana, Notion, Monday.com, or similar).
  • Communication: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills; ability to interact confidently with high-level stakeholders and board members.

Candidates who do not tick all the boxes are still encouraged to apply, those with less experience will still be considered for the position but with an adjustment to the level of seniority.

descriptions.job-11nde6p:
DRW is a diversified trading firm with over 3 decades of experience bringing sophisticated technology and exceptional people together to operate in markets around the world. We value autonomy and the ability to quickly pivot to capture opportunities, so we operate using our own capital and trading at our own risk.

Headquartered in Chicago with offices throughout the U.S., Canada, Europe, and Asia, we trade a variety of asset classes including Fixed Income, ETFs, Equities, FX, Commodities and Energy across all major global markets. We have also leveraged our expertise and technology to expand into three non-traditional strategies: real estate, venture capital and cryptoassets.

We operate with respect, curiosity and open minds. The people who thrive here share our belief that it’s not just what we do that matters–it's how we do it. DRW is a place of high expectations, integrity, innovation and a willingness to challenge consensus.

The Team:

As AI tools drive immense value across the firm, our organization faces a "Dual Mandate": providing low-friction access to the best frontier AI tools while strictly managing an exponentially growing cost curve. The unified AI Platform Team builds the centralized software, operations, and governance layers that safely route users to the most cost-effective models.

The Role:

We are looking for a Platform Engineer to help build and operationalize our AI tooling ecosystem. Working closely with the Team Lead and Senior/Staff SWE, you will be the hands-on integrator connecting external cloud AI providers, internal models, and end-user tools into our unified control plane.

Key Responsibilities

  • Configure and manage multi-engine API gateways, implementing dynamic routing rules, rate limits, and fallback logic for LLM requests.
  • Execute the technical migration and integration of firm-wide tools into our centralized management plane to ensure all AI traffic is securely logged and governed.
  • Operate within our Shared Responsibility Model alongside the Cloud team to manage AI services deployed in enterprise landing zones (e.g., managing Azure OpenAI instances, model deployments, and API key generation).
  • Write robust Go and Python code to support the continuous sync loop for our usage dashboard and implement automated "progressive friction" mechanisms, such as alerts.
  • Partner with the Inference Infrastructure pod to ensure our self-hosted, on-premise models are successfully registered and routable within our AI gateways.

Required Qualifications:

  • Strong backend programming experience, specifically in Go and/or Python.
  • Hands-on experience with API design, integration, and platform/cloud engineering concepts.
  • Familiarity with API gateways, proxy configuration, or distributed system networking.
  • A strong interest in the rapidly evolving LLM ecosystem and the technical mechanics of AI tooling.
  • A collaborative mindset with a focus on writing clean, maintainable code to replace prototype systems.

For more information about DRW's processing activities and our use of job applicants' data, please view our Privacy Notice at https://drw.com/privacy-notice.

California residents, please review the California Privacy Notice for information about certain legal rights at https://drw.com/california-privacy-notice.

OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves.
Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er. About the team

  • As a key digital asset hub, Singapore is an integral part of our global strategy. Licensed by MAS, OKX SG is focused on providing Singapore users with a secure and user-friendly platform for trading digital assets.
  • The Commercial team is responsible for developing and deepening relationships with high-value individual and institutional clients, understanding their needs, and connecting them with relevant products and solutions across the OKX ecosystem.

This includes ensuring RMs are well prepared for client conversations, agreed actions are completed promptly, and client requests are handled with care and professionalism across Product, Operations, Compliance, and other internal teams.

    - Support RMs with research and preparation for prospective high-value clients, including understanding their business, trading or investment needs, and relevant market developments.
    - Support prospect follow-up and progression through the sales process, coordinating agreed next steps and maintaining momentum.
    - Where appropriate, support targeted outreach and initial client engagement under the direction of RMs.

  • Strong interest in crypto and financial markets, with the curiosity and ability to develop deep product knowledge quickly.
  • Commercially minded and confident engaging directly with clients, with the ambition to develop into an independent Relationship Manager.
  • Experience supporting HNW/UHNW, family-office, institutional or other sophisticated clients, including complex account structures and time-sensitive instructions.
  • Strong ownership and follow-through, with the ability to manage multiple client requests and ensure issues are driven through to resolution.

Operating at the intersection of traditional finance and  cutting-edge technology, FalconX addresses the industry's foremost challenges: Navigating the digital asset market can be complex and fragmented, with limited products and services that support trading strategies, structures, and liquidity found in conventional financial markets. As a comprehensive solution for all digital asset strategies from start to scale, FalconX operates as the connective tissue empowering clients with seamless navigation through the ever- evolving cryptocurrency landscape.

About the Role

We are seeking a Finance Associate  to join our Technical Accounting & Financial Reporting team. In this role, you will be responsible for preparing full-fledged financial statements from scratch, managing technical accounting matters, and supporting M&A accounting transactions. The ideal candidate brings a strong Big 4 advisory background, deep domain knowledge in financial services and products, and a proactive mindset.

Key Responsibilities

  • Financial Statement Preparation: Draft and prepare complete end-to-end USGAAP and IFRS financial statements from scratch, including Balance Sheets, Income Statements (P&L), Notes to Accounts and relevant Disclosures.
  •  Statutory Reporting & Compliances: Ensure compliance with applicable statutory accounting frameworks and technical standards.
  • Technical Accounting: Handle complex accounting treatments and technical disclosures related to financial instruments and financial products.
  • M&A & Deal Accounting: Support M&A accounting activities, business combinations, and special accounting projects.
  • Systems & Process Improvement: Assist with reporting platform enhancements and system implementation initiatives.

  • Experience: 2–4+ years of relevant experience in technical accounting and financial reporting.
  • Firm Background: Big 4 experience is strongly preferred, with a focus on client advisory or technical accounting consulting (rather than standard financial audit).
  • Domain Knowledge: Strong background in Financial Services, with hands-on understanding of financial instruments and complex financial products.

  • Prior exposure to accounting advisory services or M&A transaction support.

descriptions.job-1h3w4y9:
About Jito


Jito builds the market layer of Solana: the execution, capital, and incentive infrastructure behind the network's onchain economy. That includes the validator client running the majority of Solana stake, BAM (a new framework for verifiable ordering, pre-execution privacy, and programmable blockspace), JitoSOL (the leading liquid staking token on Solana), and JTX (trading built directly on our own market infrastructure).

We are a lean, high-density team. Everyone here owns real surface area, works in the open, and ships at pace. The engineers on this team are the people market makers call when milliseconds matter.

About Jito

Jito builds the Market Layer of Solana: the execution systems, capital markets, and incentive mechanisms that power real markets on-chain.

Our products process billions in daily transaction value. The Jito-Solana validator client runs on the vast majority of Solana's active stake. BAM is redefining how blocks get built. JitoSOL is the leading liquid staking token on the network. We are not building at the margins. We are building core infrastructure that Solana's economy runs on.

Now we're moving up the stack, bringing that same infrastructure advantage to products that traders and users interact with directly.

We're a team of around 50 people with product-market fit across multiple product lines and years of runway. We take hard problems seriously and move fast on them. Nothing is out of reach.

About the Role

We've gone from one main product line to four, and the security work on those products has outgrown the one person doing it. This role owns product and protocol security: the surface where our code meets real money.

You'll report to the Head of Security and work alongside an Enterprise Security Engineer who owns internal infrastructure, identity and detection. The split is deliberate. They secure how we work; you secure what we ship.

This is an engineering role. Most of the backlog is code, not policy.

What You'll Own

  • Product and protocol security reviews: threat modeling, secure design review, whitebox code review, and getting in early enough to change designs rather than document them

  • Deployment hardening across our product lines, including the jito-solana deploy process

  • Ongoing internal audits of our own products rather than waiting for an external engagement to surface issues

  • Onchain monitoring: standing up tooling like Hypernative or Blockaid and building the detections that catch probing before an attack is underway

  • Bug bounty operations as we bring more of the program in-house: triage, severity assessment, remediation tracking, and escalation

  • Auditor findings driven through to closure: reviewed, prioritized, assigned, tracked

  • AI-assisted security testing and continuous scanning, plus the security surface that comes with agents and AI tooling operating inside a codebase

  • High-impact key and asset risks: key hygiene, hot wallet and engineering keys, multisigs, security councils

What We're Looking For

  • A software engineering background is essential. You've built production systems, and that foundation shapes how you approach security.

  • You've since moved into product security and are fluent across the lifecycle: threat modeling, secure design review, whitebox code review, and vulnerability testing

  • 5+ years of professional experience, with a meaningful portion in software engineering before moving into security

  • Proficiency in at least one systems or backend language. Rust preferred; Go, C++, or Python also work. You will read production codebases and build tooling as routine parts of this job.

  • Demonstrated experience in product or application security, not solely infrastructure or compliance work

  • A track record of building security tooling or automation from scratch

  • Experience running or contributing to a bug bounty program, or a clear view of how you'd run one

  • Genuine interest in AI security, including adversarial testing of agent controls

  • Strong written communication. Findings nobody can act on are findings that don't get fixed.

  • Comfortable with high ownership and working autonomously on a small team

  • Experience in web3, crypto, or DeFi

Nice to Have

  • Smart contract or onchain security experience, particularly on Solana or another SVM chain

  • Experience with onchain monitoring tooling such as Hypernative or Blockaid

  • Familiarity with validator or consensus infrastructure

  • Experience with multisig schemes: signing policy design, quorum configuration, or key management in production

  • Familiarity with hardware security modules: integration, key lifecycle, or operational use

  • Exposure to trusted execution environments: attestation, confidential compute, or secure enclave design

  • Experience with fuzzing, formal verification, or property-based testing of financial logic

Why This Role Exists

Security at Jito has been one person covering four product lines, an expanding AI surface, and a validator client running most of Solana's stake. That person has been spending their time on the most likely risks, which means the highest-impact ones get less attention than they deserve.

We're hiring two engineers so that ownership is distributed rather than bottlenecked, and so losing one person doesn't cost the whole function. The goal is not more approval steps. It is safer defaults, earlier input, and engineering that moves faster because security is in the room rather than at the gate.

How we work


Remote-first, writing-heavy, and transparent by default: most decisions happen in public Slack channels, and everyone's voice carries. We value ownership, humility, curiosity, and getting it done over getting it perfect. Small egos, high standards.


What we offer


Competitive compensation including salary and token incentives, the tools you need to do your best work, and a seat at the center of Solana's market infrastructure alongside some of the strongest engineers in the ecosystem.

Jito is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate candidates on the basis of their skills, experience, and potential contribution, without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

You'll work directly with leadership and the Head of Finance, with real ownership over the processes you run. Our processes are established, and you'll be trusted to own them, improve them where it makes sense, and take on challenging problems across a fast-moving group of companies.

What is Kalshi?

Kalshi has defined a new category: prediction markets. Kalshi allows people to trade on the outcome of any events and turn any question about the future into a financial asset. Kalshi fought for years and legalized prediction markets in the US for the first time in history, is currently the fastest growing financial market in America, and has thousands of markets across politics, economics, financials, weather, tech, AI, culture and more.

We believe prediction markets have the potential to be the largest financial market because they turn anything into a financial position.

  • Our vision: well… build the largest financial market on the planet.

  • Our mission: bring more truth to the world through the power of markets.

Our culture is simple: we hire really talented people, work really hard, and enjoy the climb. We are looking for ambitious and exceptional people to join our (relatively small) team to help us build the next generation of financial markets.

Role Roadmap

We’re looking for a Growth PM to own how we bring dormant users back to Kalshi.

People come to Kalshi for events they care about - a sports season, an election, or a major cultural moment. When those events end, we need to give them compelling reasons to return. You’ll own the product strategy and execution behind that work: understanding why users become inactive, identifying opportunities to bring them back, and building programs that turn renewed interest into sustained trading activity.

This is a deeply analytical, hands-on role. You’ll spend significant time in SQL, studying user behavior and translating what you learn into experiments. Working closely with engineering, lifecycle marketing, and acquisition teams, you’ll test product experiences, incentives, audiences, and timing to find what works. Over time, you’ll build a repeatable reactivation playbook and help users discover reasons to trade across multiple categories.

What You’ll Do

  • Set the roadmap, prioritize opportunities, and take experiments from analysis through launch and measurement.

  • Use SQL to analyze cohorts by sports season, category traded, major event, and behavior. Identify churn patterns and size opportunities.

  • Test product experiences, incentives, and other approaches, with clear hypotheses and rigorous measurement.

  • Develop reactivation strategies for seasonal sports, elections, and other major moments, including what happens after they end.

  • Determine which users to reach, what will resonate, and when to engage them. Coordinate channel execution and measurement.

  • Build ways for users to find relevant markets beyond the event or sport that first brought them to Kalshi.

  • Turn successful experiments into ongoing programs, document what works, and establish benchmarks for reactivation performance.

  • Track post-season reactivation rates, the share of active traders who have reactivated, and whether returning users stay engaged. Coordinate proposed programs with the CCO and CRO.

What You Bring

  • Experience as a Growth PM or consumer Product Manager, with a track record of using data and experimentation to improve user behavior and business outcomes.

  • Strong, hands-on SQL skills. You can independently explore user data, build cohort analyses, and turn findings into clear product decisions.

  • Excellent quantitative judgment, including the ability to size opportunities, prioritize experiments, and distinguish meaningful results from noise.

  • Strong execution and ownership. You can move from an ambiguous problem to a launched experiment and follow through on the results.

  • Creative thinking about why users return to a product, with ideas that extend beyond standard promotional offers.

  • An understanding of sports and seasonality, including how fan interest changes throughout the calendar.

  • The ability to work closely with engineering, lifecycle marketing, and acquisition teams to deliver coordinated programs.

NYC Pay Transparency Disclosure

Salary Range: $150,000–$250,000 annually, plus equity and benefits. This range reflects current market data for this role. Kalshi has minimal hierarchy and broad variance in experience levels within each title; if your compensation expectations exceed this range, we encourage you to reach out - we’re always happy to discuss

Our Culture

Meritocracy is at our core, and we value people who take ownership and figure (usually hard) things out. We dream big. We love our craft deeply and are proud of what we put out in the world. We are committed to our vision of building something big… but also useful: a product that brings more truth through the power of markets.

Kalshians are Kalshi’s most important asset: we pick Kalshians carefully, so we trust them fully on day 1.

Commitment to Equal Opportunity

Kalshi is committed to creating a culture of inclusion and belonging, and we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We believe it is our collective responsibility to uphold these values and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to join us in our mission. All qualified applicants will be treated with respect and receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, uniform service, veteran status, age, or any other protected characteristic per federal, state, or local law. If you are passionate about what you do and want to use your talents to support our mission and values, we’d love to hear from you.

ABOUT THE ROLE
The Controls SME is Managed Services' controls and automation expert, embedded in a data center build. The role supports design review, vendor oversight, and commissioning to make sure the control systems are operable, maintainable, and trustworthy at turnover. Controls are the facility's nervous system: when they fail or mislead, operators lose sight of everything else.

Some of the key responsibilities you should expect are the following:

Operability Design Review
Review controls designs, including BMS/BAS, EPMS, SCADA, PLC-based plant controls, CDU and cooling plant controls, and generator, UPS, and switchgear controller integration, through an operations lens. Sequences of operations, failure-mode and fail-safe behavior, loss-of-network and loss-of-controller response, manual and local override, point lists and instrumentation adequacy, alarm philosophy and prioritization, graphics clarity, and OT network architecture and access control. Push back where the design assumes an operator will understand or recover something the system never tells them.


Controls QA/QC and Vendor Oversight
Provide QA/QC oversight of controls scope for new construction and retrofits: review vendor proposals and programming, directly oversee system configuration and component upgrades, and witness factory tests. Hold controls vendors to Hut 8 standards and to the approved sequences, and make sure every modification to a system follows change control.


Construction-Phase Verification
Walk controls installations at key milestones. Flag operability and quality issues to the MEP superintendent early, while they are still cheap to fix.


Commissioning
Witness Level 3-5 commissioning of controls and automation: point-to-point verification, sequence- of-operations testing, controller, server, and network failover, alarm verification, trend validation, and integrated systems testing across mechanical, electrical, and controls, including loss-of- communication and loss-of-BMS scenarios. Review programming through the commissioning process, drive operational findings into the Cx log with clear acceptance criteria, and verify closure personally.


Turnover Readiness
Verify controls turnover packages: as-built sequences of operation, point lists, control and network drawings, programming backups and configuration files under version control, licenses and credentials transferred to Hut 8, alarm setpoint and priority matrices, trend baselines, spare controllers and critical modules, and PM program inputs such as backup routines, firmware updates, and panel power health. Confirm the backups actually restore.


Training
Provide technical controls training and support to Facility Operations staff, and validate that operator training equips the team to use the systems, not just look at them.


Program Feedback
Feed operational lessons into Hut 8 controls standards, point naming and alarm conventions, and the next project's basis of design, and work with other Hut 8 sites and teams to carry standards across the portfolio.

ABOUT YOU
What we're looking for:

  • 7+ years of controls experience in programming, start-up, and commissioning of complex systems such as central plants, air handling units, and evaporative cooling and humidification systems. A bachelor's degree or trade certification in a related field plus 3+ years of controls industry experience will be considered in lieu.
  • Experience in critical environments, with a working knowledge of critical facility operations and procedure-based work.
  • Theoretical and practical understanding of control equipment and systems: design, maintenance, troubleshooting, testing, and construction.
  • Working knowledge of the mechanical, electrical, and life safety systems found in critical facilities.
  • Sequence-of-operations fluency: you can read one critically, catch the gaps and failure modes, and test whether it behaves as written.
  • Experience interpreting blueprints, CAD drawings, and controls diagrams.
  • Turnover documentation rigor, especially programming backups, configuration files, and version control.
  • Comfortable embedded with a construction team while holding the operations line, and effective in a highly collaborative, cross-functional environment.

Preferred:

  • Data center experience.
  • PLC programming experience
  • IT or networking certification
  • Equipment field service engineering or manufacturer representative experience.
  • Demonstrated use of AI tools to improve workflows with measurable results, such as efficiency gains or quality improvements.

ABOUT THE WORK ENVIRONMENT

  • Full time on-site role.
descriptions.job-0v778k1:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Product Support team directly supports our largest and fastest growing users, partnering with them to grow their business. We actively seek and capitalize on opportunities to meet and exceed their service expectations, working to impress the trendsetters and remove obstacles from their path. The team is there when users need us but also there proactively - before they even realize they need support. The Critical Support  team exists within Product Support to help address the most escalated user issues. This team responds to users who have sent their issue or concerns to a member of their Stripe account team or to a Stripe executive. We own the resolution of the immediate issue at hand, as well as ensuring that the factors that led to the escalation are addressed and remediated. 

Ultimately, these cases often shine a light on points of failures within Stripe, and the team has the opportunity to create transformative user experiences, while also helping edit Stripe to rectify the structural issues that resulted in the escalation in the first place. This is a high visibility, high impact role, with the responsibility to work with executives users and cross functional stakeholders, all while helping shape the evolution of this team. 

What you’ll do

We are looking for a strategic leader to continue to build and lead Critical Support as Stripe’s ultimate.  You will own the strategy, operating model, and cross-functional partnerships that enable Stripe to resolve the most severe and consequential user issues with urgency, judgment, and lasting impact on Stripe’s product and processes.  You will equally wear a strategic and operational hat.  You  will lead a high performing team of escalations specialists to deliver exceptional user experiences. This team goes beyond basic troubleshooting—it's about  developing a team of product and process expertise with analytical mindset and project management skills to strategically improve our support systems, processes, and product quality. You will play a key role to cultivate the happiness of their team through clear goal setting, feedback mechanism, mentoring, and advocacy within the organization. 

Responsibilities

  • Guide the organization to design and deliver scalable user support by partnering effectively with cross functional stakeholders across Product, Engineering and broader teams such Sales (Go-To-Market), Risk etc as needed
  • Co-own & drive Critical Support strategy, operating model, and multi-quarter roadmap development that meets or exceeds Stripe’s users and internal stakeholders expectations towards critical support experience 
  • Act as a trusted partner to Sales, Account Management, Product, Engineering, Risk, and executive leadership during high-stakes user situations.
  • Drive strong operational delivery and process improvement helping to mitigate risk while balancing operational efficiency and user impact
  • Maintain metrics and analysis of team performance, and provide regular reporting on team performance in the form of written analysis and performance reports
  • Develop strong ties with cross-functional teams and position the Critical Support team to act as ultimate unblocking force for users as well as source of the insights on Stripe’s product and process.  
  • Set clear goals and directions, and provide regular feedback on team members’ performance
  • Ensure team members are happy, effective, and growing in their career and new work experiences
  • Transmit and foster our values, serving as a beacon of Stripe’s user-centric philosophy and culture of transparency, empathy, inclusion, and empowerment
  • Help build the organization through management projects such as recruiting, training, writing team policies, defining team processes, or other organizational improvements

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • At least 8+ years of direct people management experience; including senior front line specialists and/or managers and supported them to career growth and transitions 
  • Experience leading operational teams such as product support teams (preferably in high-growth technology companies)
  • Experience in strategizing and driving large scale operational process improvements and program management work
  • Solid experience in stakeholder management, with the ability to influence cross-functional teams and drive progress for the team and users
  • Strong analytical sense and track-record of making data driven decisions
  • Skill and credibility doing the core work of a user facing team with a high bar for quality and a willingness to lead by example and get into the details of front-line work if required
  • Strong ownership mindset and experience in driving highly complex initiatives at speed 
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills

Preferred qualifications

  • Prior experience with Escalations, Incident Management 
  • Comfort with some technical troubleshooting
  • Familiarity with FinTech industry and products
  • Passion for learning new functions and features of technical products
descriptions.job-1vcblw1:
This role is intended for current high school students graduating in 2027 or later.

 

Who we are 

About Stripe

Stripe is a technology company focused on improving the conditions for economic growth and prosperity. We build programmable financial infrastructure, rethinking from first principles how financial services should work, to make it easier and cheaper for any business to start and scale. More than 10 million businesses build on Stripe, spanning the economic frontier, from solo founders to established enterprises, united by a practical focus on growth. The most ambitious companies in the world use Stripe as core infrastructure to grow faster. They process trillions of dollars a year on Stripe, equivalent to around 1.6% of global GDP. While economic growth makes everyone better off, open markets also enable greater variety. When any business can easily serve a global customer base, the quality and diversity of products in the world increase, and craft and creativity are unleashed into the smallest niches.

Our own growth is wholly contingent on the success of the businesses building on Stripe. We therefore invest back into our technology at an unusual rate. We make upgrades to our products every single day to deliver compounding gains to our customers. We maintain some of the most reliable APIs on the internet. We build entirely new pieces of financial infrastructure to enable new ideas. And our significant advances in risk and fraud infrastructure over many years are making the internet economy safer and more accessible.

Though people at Stripe do not tend to take themselves seriously, Stripe is a fairly serious place: our customers are depending on us for their livelihoods. We admire ambition, intensity, curiosity, humility, and rigor. The most effective people become knowledgeable about many domains besides their own. Any company is an applied exercise in understanding some aspect of society or the market. In working with so many, especially the new and innovative ones, we think that Stripe is one of the very best places to learn about how the world works.

What you’ll do

This is a small, selective internship for exceptional high school students and recent graduates whose technical work already stands out well beyond what we typically see at this stage. We are not looking for potential or credentials alone. We are looking for students who can show, through what they have built, researched, or contributed, that they are ready to do substantive engineering work with a Stripe team.
You will spend 12 consecutive weeks between May and August working in person from Stripe’s San Francisco or Seattle office on a scoped engineering project. You will own a problem end to end with support from your manager and teammates, contribute to Stripe’s codebase, and learn how engineers build reliable systems used by millions of businesses. Recent Stripe intern projects include expanding Payments Foundation Model capabilities to improve generalized anomaly detection, building more approachable fraud controls, creating safer payouts, and developing user-facing solutions that prevent costly pricing mistakes and make merchant checkout setup easier.

You will work alongside Stripe’s collegiate interns and full-time employees. That means participating in the same team environment, learning how engineers at different stages approach technical decisions, and building relationships across the broader Stripe community.

This is not a trainee or classroom-based program. You will receive support from your manager and teammates, but you will be expected to contribute to your team’s work, learn quickly, communicate clearly, ask strong questions, and produce work that holds up under technical review.

As with Stripe’s collegiate internships, strong performance may lead to consideration for future opportunities at Stripe, including full-time employment for interns who meet the relevant eligibility and hiring requirements. Future opportunities are not guaranteed and will depend on individual performance and Stripe’s hiring needs.

Responsibilities

  • Participate fully in the team you join, including team discussions, decisions, and the technical design process.
  • Write, test, and document software intended for production use by Stripe teams and users.
  • Give and receive technical feedback through code reviews and design discussions.
  • Collaborate with engineers and cross-functional partners to seek and incorporate feedback.
  • Learn unfamiliar systems through independent research and close work with your manager, mentor, teammates, and subject matter experts.
  • Communicate the status of your work clearly, including progress, risks, open questions, and where you need help.
  • Use current AI development tools thoughtfully while applying rigorous judgment to review, refine, test, and validate outputs.

What We Look For

We don't have a test score threshold. We look for people who have already started acting like the engineers and operators we most admire.

  • Ambitious builder: You are energized by building solutions without a clear precedent and working through difficult technical problems. You can point to technical work that shows unusual initiative, depth, or originality for someone at your stage.
  • Rigorous thinker: You care about whether your work is correct, not just whether it runs. You test your assumptions, examine edge cases, and can explain the choices you made.
  • Adaptable problem solver: You learn quickly, respond well to feedback, and keep making progress when the path is unclear.
  • Collaborative teammate: You communicate clearly, treat others with kindness, and know when to work independently and when to ask for help.

Minimum requirements

  • Currently enrolled in high school, or graduating from high school before the internship begins.
  • Available to work full-time and in person from Stripe’s San Francisco or Seattle office for 12 consecutive weeks during a mutually agreed period between May and August 2027. We cannot accommodate remote participation, a shorter internship, or breaks within the 12-week period.
  • Experience programming through independent projects, research, coursework, competitions, open source contributions, a startup, or another setting. We work mostly in Ruby, Java, JavaScript, Go, and Scala. We believe new programming languages can be learned when the fundamentals are strong.
  • Evidence of exceptional technical achievement for your stage. This could include a product or system you built, a substantial open source contribution, original research, meaningful work at a startup, advanced competition performance, or another body of work that demonstrates comparable depth and ownership.
  • Ability to explain your individual contribution to the work you submit, including the problem, technical decisions, tradeoffs, testing, feedback, and what you would improve.
  • Experience working with others on a technical project and incorporating feedback from peers, mentors, teachers, users, or collaborators.
  • Ability to learn unfamiliar systems through independent research and work with a mentor or subject matter expert.
  • Clear written and verbal communication.
  • Ability to meet the employment eligibility, minimum age, and documentation requirements for the role’s location by the internship start date. Final contract language is subject to Legal review.

Preferred qualifications

The Principal reports to the FP&A leader, who retains overall coordination and escalation responsibility. Business-unit and process assignments may evolve as the team and businesses grow.

• Business partnership: Serve as the day-to-day finance partner for assigned business units. Understand operating drivers, commitments, headcount, capital needs, and risks; support leaders with timely analysis and clear recommendations.

State the business need and acceptance criteria for BI/IT/AI work; collaborate on integrations and technical changes with the designated system owners. Use NetSuite as a financial data source subject to Accounting controls.

• Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field; FP&A, CFA Certificates preferred

• Strong business judgment and ability to prioritize, operate independently, and deliver through ambiguity and change.
• Executive-level communication and influence skills, with a record of building credibility
across functions.

This role is in office at our corporate headquarters in the Brickell area of Miami, Florida. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

descriptions.job-14kw575:
The 4 biggest blockchain strengths are also its weakness

  • Permissionless nature leads to fragmentation of meaning

  • Decentralization leads to too many standards

  • Immutability leads to exponential data + query infrastructure complexity

  • Neutrality means that no one is accountable for interpretations

Blockchain data is public. It is not usable at institutional scale. Despite being open, blockchain data is fragmented, hard to interpret, and painful to maintain. Even a simple question like “Who are the largest Ethereum token holders over time?” can require running nodes, ingesting full chain history, decoding contracts, cleaning edge cases, and writing complex SQL.

Blockchains are optimized for writes, not reads.

They are built for consensus and execution, not searchability, standardization, or financial interpretation. Blockchains are computers, not databases. Every protocol defines its own schema. The same economic action can be encoded in dozens of different ways. The result:

  • Fragmented standards

  • Exponential complexity

  • No accountability for interpretation

  • Events without economic meaning

Finance cannot operate on that, it needs an effective system of record.

Allium is building the System of Record for Onchain Finance

Allium ingests, verifies, and standardizes data across 140+ blockchains and 30+ petabytes of history. We close four structural gaps that prevent blockchains from becoming systems of record:

  • Semantic Gap: Translating raw events into financial concepts like payments, trades, deposits, and staking income

  • Standardization Gap: Mapping thousands of protocols into a single canonical cross chain schema

  • Infrastructure Gap: Read optimized, globally distributed data at web scale

  • Accountability Gap: Auditable methodology, SLAs, and SOC 1 and 2 compliance

The result is a neutral, canonical data layer institutions can build on with confidence.

Finance is moving onchain

Stablecoins, tokenized assets, trading, staking, and lending are growing rapidly. Institutions need a trusted source of truth for onchain financial activity, just as they rely on Bloomberg or DTCC in traditional markets. Raw blockchains cannot serve that role.

As AI agents begin transacting autonomously, the requirement becomes even stricter. Agents cannot reason over raw event logs. They need structured data, attribution, condition checks, and auditability.

Allium is the read layer that makes onchain finance usable for humans and machines.

Who We Serve

Allium powers three core personas with the same canonical data foundation:

1. Finance, Accounting, and Risk Teams They need reliable, audit grade answers. They rely on Allium for financial reporting, reconciliation, compliance, risk monitoring, and defensible metrics that can stand up to auditors and regulators.

2. Engineers and Product Teams They need low latency, production ready infrastructure. They use Allium to power wallets, trading systems, payment rails, staking infrastructure, and real time applications that cannot break.

3. Strategy, Research, and Executive Teams They need clarity and insight. They use Allium to understand ecosystem economics, market structure, user behavior, competitive dynamics, and where capital is flowing onchain.

And of course...agents 🦞. Our customers and users include Visa, Stripe, G-SIB Banks, Big 4 Accounting firms, BCG, Coinbase, Phantom, Uniswap and cited by the Federal Reserve.

About the role

You’ll own our day-to-day legal work and build the practices that support Allium as we grow. Your initial focus will be commercial contracts, data licensing, and technology transactions. Data rights are central to our business: permitted use, redistribution, derived data, and AI all shape what we can build and how we serve customers.

You’ll work closely with our founders and leaders across Finance, Sales, Product, and Engineering, with outside counsel available for specialist matters and additional capacity. This role suits someone who enjoys personally drafting and negotiating agreements while building a legal function at a Series B startup. You’ll have substantial ownership from the start and a direct role in how Allium builds products, structures partnerships, and serves customers.

What you’ll do

  • Lead commercial contracting. Draft and negotiate enterprise customer agreements, data licenses, partnerships, and vendor contracts. Work with Sales and Finance to resolve issues and move deals through to signature.

  • Shape our data and IP rights. Establish practical positions on data acquisition, permitted use, redistribution, derived data, AI use, and post-termination rights. Align supplier rights with the commitments we make to customers.

  • Advise on products and partnerships. Work with Product and Engineering early on new offerings. Translate privacy, IP, and regulatory considerations into clear recommendations that help teams make decisions.

  • Build legal operations. Develop templates, negotiation playbooks, approval guidelines, intake workflows, and a reliable contract repository. Use AI and automation thoughtfully, with appropriate confidentiality protections and human review.

  • Coordinate broader legal needs. Partner with leadership and outside counsel on corporate governance, financings, employment matters, compliance, and other issues as they arise. Manage priorities, specialist support, and legal spend.

  • Make obligations actionable. Help teams understand the commitments in our contracts and policies, and work with the right owners to put them into practice.

What we’re looking for

  • Strong experience independently leading complex commercial negotiations for a technology, SaaS, financial data, or related business.

  • Depth in data licensing or technology transactions, including IP rights, data use, confidentiality, liability, indemnification, and privacy provisions.

  • Experience advising business teams directly, ideally in-house, and translating legal analysis into clear decisions and workable alternatives.

  • A track record of building or improving legal templates, playbooks, and processes, with sound judgment about when to push and when to bring in specialist counsel.

  • Clear writing, strong negotiation skills, and trusted working relationships with technical and commercial teams.

  • Ownership and adaptability: you can manage competing priorities, follow through on details, and create structure while staying close to the work.

  • A J.D. or equivalent legal qualification and active admission to a U.S. state bar, with eligibility to practice in-house in the role’s location.

Experience that would be helpful

  • Working in a small legal team or helping build a legal function.

  • Financial market data, fintech, payments, AI, or blockchain-related products.

  • Selling to financial institutions or other sophisticated enterprise buyers.

  • Privacy, product counseling, or public-sector contracting.

Don't take our word for it, what our customers say about us (https://www.allium.so/blog#love)

What some cool people have to say about us:

  • The Information's Top 50 Startups (https://www.allium.so/post/allium-named-to-the-informations-50-most-promising-startups-of-2025)

  • Mario Gabriele from The Generalist's Future 50 Startup List: https://www.allium.so/post/allium-named-awardee-of-the-generalists-inaugural-future-50-startups

  • Tomasz Tungus from Theory Ventures: https://tomtunguz.com/allium/

  • Bucky Moore from Kleiner Perkins: https://www.kleinerperkins.com/perspectives/allium-series-a/

Ok, now for some tough love. Here are the values we strive for at Allium:

  • Obsessiveness - The best people at Allium cannot put a problem down once they pick it up. We care more about the work than is strictly rational. Institutions trust us because our data is right. Right means caring about the small things. The decoded contract that ships with one wrong field. The label that is 99% accurate but wrong on the address that matters. The query that runs in 4 seconds when it should run in 400 milliseconds. Most companies tolerate these. We do not.

    Obsessiveness shows up as depth of care. It is not measured in hours worked or visible effort. You should feel something physical when work ships half-right. That instinct is what we hire for.

  • Pro Athlete Mindset - Consistency. Day in and day out, in pursuit of excellence. A win yesterday does not guarantee (or even imply!) a win tomorrow. I hope anyone who supports a failing sports team will feel the pain (cough Man United fans) of inconsistency

  • Figure It Out & Extreme Ownership - Every day is unexplored territory. There are new engineering frameworks, new legal docs, new compliance, new sales, new regulations, and new operational procedures every single day. If you don’t know it, learn it. If you can’t learn it, find someone or a product that does it. If you can’t find someone, find someone who can find someone. It is never a lack of resources, but lack of resourcefulness.

  • High Agency - (One of) the highest commonalities between all successful people is their responsiveness. Most successful billionaire CEOs still reply to emails within minutes (within working hours). And when you reply, respond fast with effective solutions - and even better, resolutions. If you’re looking for a superpower, you can’t go wrong with responsiveness. Well of course this doesn't make sense when you're an engineer coding in flow, but in general high agency of problem solving gets one very far in life

  • Leading from the Front - No one is going to listen (and adopt) your suggestion unless you lead by example. It’s one thing to say We need to do XYZ this better & it’s another thing to build an MVP and say “This is the way we should do things”. The proof of work and momentum goes a long way.

  • Strong Opinions On the Future (loosely held) - It is okay to be wrong, but what is not okay is not to have an idea of how a better future should be. Alliumites take pride in trying to improving everything about the company all the time.

  • Sense of (Allium) business smell - There are number of folks who live to eat at Allium, but the Allium smell we are talking about is that we love folks who naturally want to know why and how the work they are doing builds leverage for their teammates and also relates to the business goals

About the team

We invite people of all backgrounds (https://www.allium.so/about). We have engineers who learnt coding much later in life, who learnt coding on the side, we have engineers who are still in school and we also have engineers who went to the top schools (CMU, Stanford, UIUC, UPenn, Oxford, NUS, Cornell), all are welcome if one comes in with a curious mind and an infectious work ethic.

Administrative Benefits

  • Medical, Dental, Vision, Life and AD&D insurance - US folks get 100% coverage for Gold plans, 80% for dependents

  • Ownership - Meaningful early-stage equity. Every full-time employee receives a stock option grant so you can share directly in Allium's upside

  • Time off - Flexible, trust-based paid time off. We encourage people to take the rest they need. In every country we hire, our policies meet or exceed local statutory vacation requirements

  • Retirement - Company sponsored 401(k) plan in US so you can save pre-tax for the long term

All applicants have to answer this pop quiz: "What is an Allium? What is your favorite Allium?". Bonus points for the right pronunciation.

Join us in building the future of finance.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world's biggest financial problems. We're looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn't a place for complacency, it's where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We're a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards.

The Developer Infrastructure org is the engine behind Robinhood's entire engineering organization — a collection of tightly integrated teams whose collective mission is to make every engineer at Robinhood faster, more reliable, and exponentially more productive. The org spans four major teams: DevX (Developer Experience), TestX (Test Infrastructure), Backend Platform, and Mobile Platform. DevX owns Robinhood's monorepo and Bazel-based build infrastructure — the critical layer between a developer writing code and that code being ready to ship — along with the company's full CI/CD pipeline and remote build execution cluster. TestX owns the infrastructure behind Robinhood's entire test experience: the integration test environments, and personal development environments that serve as miniature simulations of the full Robinhood system, giving engineers a safe, isolated space to test their code end-to-end before it ever touches production. Backend Platform and Mobile Platform own the core language runtimes, libraries, IDEs, and developer toolchains across Python, Go, TypeScript, Swift, and Android. Together, these teams share a single north star: leveraging AI and agentic systems to fundamentally transform Robinhood's software development lifecycle — making every engineer dramatically more productive and the entire org a force multiplier for the business.

As the Senior Staff Software Engineer, Developer Infrastructure, you are the technical driver of this entire org — the Uber Tech Lead unifying DevX, TestX, Backend Platform, and Mobile Platform under one cohesive technical vision. Your primary focus will be DevX, owning the technical direction of Robinhood's most critical build and developer infrastructure. But your influence stretches far wider: you will be a driving force in weaving AI and agentic development deeply into every layer of the software development lifecycle — from intelligent code review and automated build pipelines to agentic coding systems that multiply what each engineer can ship. This is a rare opportunity to shape not just how Robinhood builds software today, but what engineering velocity looks like for the entire industry!

This role is based in our New York City or Menlo Park office, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week.

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.

What you’ll do

  • Lead and evolve Robinhood's Bazel-based monorepo build infrastructure — own the remote build execution cluster, drive language-agnostic build optimization across Python, Go, TypeScript, and more, and ensure fast, stable feedback loops for the entire engineering org
  • Scale CI/CD pipelines to support thousands of daily builds with speed, safety, and reliability — overseeing GitHub repository configurations, pre-merge checks, and test execution infrastructure across the company
  • Drive the vision for TestX — the test infrastructure and environments that power Robinhood's entire test experience, including integration test environments and personal development environments that simulate the full Robinhood system so engineers can test safely and confidently
  • Champion the integration of AI and agentic systems across the full software development lifecycle — driving initiatives that use intelligent automation and coding agents to multiply developer velocity, improve code quality, and accelerate the pace of innovation across the org
  • Set technical standards across Backend Platform and Mobile Platform — owning the vision for core language runtimes, libraries, IDE tooling, and developer environment security across Python, Go, TypeScript, Swift, and Android
  • Partner with engineering leadership and cross-functional stakeholders to define and execute a long-term developer infrastructure roadmap that embeds AI as a force multiplier at every layer of the SDLC

What you bring

descriptions.job-1i7qnkh:
Work from anywhere, impact everywhere 

Diversity is at the heart of who we are at Xapo Bank.
We’re a fully distributed team of over 160 Xapiens that work remotely from 50+ countries around the world.

Our beginning: A world that enjoys economic freedom and wealth protection,no matter where you live or who is running your country.
To achieve that, we search the world for the best people for the job.
We work hard, think globally, and inspire each other to learn and grow.
We are committed to changing the way things are done.

Although we are headquartered in Gibraltar, this is a full time, 100% remote position 
Work from anywhere!

Position overview

Xapo Bank is establishing a Structured Solutions function to own and expand its product offering, spanning yield products, tokenisation, asset-backed lending (ABL) workstreams, and new structures at the intersection of digital assets and traditional finance.

As Head of Structured Solutions, you will take ownership of an established, revenue-generating credit fund and the counterparty relationships that sit behind it, while setting the strategic direction for what we build next. You will report directly to the CFO, own the house view on structured product strategy, act as the primary interface with our external licensed Investment Manager and the Investment Committee, and have the mandate and budget to grow the team as the function scales.

This is a rare combination: a live book with existing counterparties, an established governance process, and dedicated analyst support from day one, alongside genuine authority to shape what Xapo Bank's structured product offering becomes and to build the team you need to deliver it. You will have a structured transition period working alongside experienced outgoing team members to absorb institutional knowledge, models, data, and counterparty context.

Credit judgement is central to this role, not a supporting activity. Counterparty selection, due diligence and ongoing monitoring are how the credit fund is managed day to day, so we need someone whose underwriting is as strong as their structuring, as credible assessing a counterparty as they are designing a payoff profile, with the judgement to walk away from a deal that prices well but underwrites badly.

In your first 12 months you will:

  • Take full ownership of the fund and its counterparty relationships, completing the knowledge transfer from the outgoing team.
  • Establish your operating rhythm with the Investment Committee and the licensed Investment Manager.
  • Set out the forward roadmap for Xapo's structured product offering and the resourcing to deliver it.

Responsibilities

Strategy and product:

  • Set the strategic direction and house view for structured investment solutions, identifying and designing new structured products for the Xapo client base.
  • Lead delivery of yield products, tokenisation initiatives, Bitcoin Backed Loans, and other new structures from concept through to launch, from payoff profile through to delivery mechanism, including regulatory consequences.
  • Responsible for driving Xapo's internal investment committee, a monthly forum with the CEO, CFO, and Head of Product, on new ideas, products, and structures.

Credit, due diligence, and risk:

FUND

  • Own comprehensive initial due diligence on prospective counterparties and ongoing due diligence on existing ones, covering counterparty financial analysis, business processes, and risk evaluation.
  • Produce credit assessments in a standardised, committee-ready format suitable for review by the licensed Investment Manager and the Investment Committee.
  • Maintain ongoing credit risk oversight of the book, ensuring positions are managed appropriately and the fund operates within its mandate at all times.
  • Set, monitor, and enforce exposure, concentration, and limit frameworks, escalating breaches and emerging risks promptly.

XAPO

  • Work alongside the Risk function on price risk and credit risk evaluation, system requirements, and regulatory consequences.

Fund Origination, execution, and relationships:

  • Identify and originate new counterparties for the fund to lend to.
  • Prepare and present due diligence and lending proposals through the Investment Committee, owning the quality and rigour of the committee process.
  • Support Legal in negotiating the fund's standard documentation with counterparties through to close.
  • Maintain and evolve counterparty relationships across the life of each facility, keeping engagement current across all commercial and operational matters.

Fund operations and stakeholder management:

  • Act as the primary point of engagement with the external licensed Investment Manager on regulated fund management activity, maintaining constant contact.
  • Oversee fund operations and accounting, liaising with the fund administrator and fund accountant to ensure NAV is struck correctly and resolving operational issues as they arise.
  • Support Xapo Operations and the fund accountant on reconciliation, ensuring everything matches correctly.
  • Allocate coin and capital inflows arising from investors sourced by Xapo.
  • Represent the fund internally, keeping the wider Xapo organisation informed on positioning, activity, and performance.

Treasury and banking input:

  • Work closely with Treasury, providing advisory input across risk evaluation, trading and execution, and system requirements.
  • Contribute banking input on ALCO, stress testing, and pricing.

Team and knowledge:

  • Build, manage, and develop the Structured Solutions team, mentoring junior analysts and expanding the bench as the function grows — you will have the mandate to shape the team's size and shape over time.
  • Enable the team: surface and resolve blockers quickly, run regular one-to-ones, and take ownership of team wellbeing.
  • Represent the team within Xapo, articulating what it needs and keeping the organisation informed.
  • Ensure institutional knowledge is documented and durable, contributing to and maintaining the investment team knowledge portal so that the function is not dependent on any single individual.
  • Act as an internal reference point for technical, market, and crypto-ecosystem questions, contributing to projects across the business where relevant.
  • During the initial transition period, work alongside outgoing senior team members to absorb institutional knowledge, models, data, and counterparty context.

Skills needed

  • Substantial experience in investment management, structured products, or digital asset markets, including senior ownership of a product, credit, or trading function.
  • Demonstrable credit underwriting and counterparty risk experience, ideally including unsecured lending, with the judgement to say no to a deal that prices well but underwrites badly.
  • The ability to diligence both sides of the market: regulated financial institutions using audited financials, capital position, and covenant analysis; and crypto-native counterparties, including the limitations of proof-of-reserves, custody and rehypothecation risk, venue and exchange exposure, on-chain analysis, and opaque cross-jurisdictional group structures.
  • Strong quantitative capability and comfort building or overseeing pricing, risk, and structuring models.
  • A track record of designing and launching new financial products, ideally spanning yield, lending, or tokenisation.
  • Experience operating through formal governance processes such as investment committees, with the judgement to know when to escalate.
  • Demonstrated people leadership: building teams, developing junior talent, and setting a clear technical and strategic direction.
  • Familiarity with both Bitcoin and traditional fiat markets, and genuine interest in where digital assets and structured finance intersect.
  • Excellent stakeholder management skills, comfortable engaging with external investment managers, counterparties, and internal committees alike.

Nice to have:

  • Exposure to regulated fund structures and working alongside a licensed external investment manager.
  • Experience with fund operations, including fund administrators, fund accountants, and the NAV process.
  • Existing relationships within digital asset counterparty or institutional investor networks.
  • Prior experience standing up or scaling a new team or function within a fintech, bank, or asset manager.
  • Balance sheet and treasury experience, including ALCO, stress testing, and pricing within a regulated credit institution.
  • Experience taking over an existing book and making it your own, rather than only building from a blank page.

Other requirements:

  • A dedicated workspace.
  • A reliable internet connection with the fastest speed possible in your area.
  • Alignment with Our Values and the Xapo Values-Driven Leadership principles.

Why work for Xapo?

Impact Globally, Work Remotely.

  • Shape the Future
    Improve lives through cutting-edge technology, work 100% remotely from anywhere in the world.

  • Great work-life balance
    Build amazing things with a balance of autonomy and collaborative teamwork. Set your own work schedule and make use of a flexible PTO plan when you need to recharge. 

  • Expect Excellence
    Collaborate, learn, and grow with a high-performance team. Learn how you learn best - from books to conferences, you’ll get a yearly budget for your individual learning and development goals.

At Xapo, we prioritize consumer protection and adhere to regulatory requirements by ensuring that all Xapiens are accountable for upholding principles of fair treatment, transparency, and ethical conduct in their interactions with customers and stakeholders.
